title: 1943: Otis White and Spike from Memphis, woodshedding 'Sweet Lorraine'
summary: Pillars hires two Memphis saxophonists and drills Otis White, who has a huge tone but reads slowly, on 'Sweet Lorraine'.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: 1943, comes on the scene. We still had the same problem, trying to get musicians. It was a job, trying to get various ones who could play shows and fill the bill. We scuffled, and I heard about a couple of saxophone players in Memphis, Tennessee. One was named Otis White and the other boy's name, we called him Spike. You know his name?
No, I dont know Spike's name.

I could never think of Spike's name. I'll have to apologize for that. It's been so long ago. They came in one morning, and before they checked in the hotel, I took them by the Club and had them tune up, and break them in on our repertoire. Spike, I found out, was a very fast reader. He could read anything. But the other saxophonist, Otis White, was the opposite. But Otis had played one of the most beautiful tones of any saxophonist I've ever heard. He had what we call a big tone, and I would say, to me, he had the biggest tone of many tones that I've heard throughout my career.

So I took Otis and we went to the woodshed, meaning that we took various tunes, bar by bar, note by note, I found out -- when I first started playing music that that was the best way, if you couldn't do it any other way. And the first tune that I picked was Sweet Lorraine." And I worked with Otis
for about four hours that day. And Otis was able to play 'Sweet Lorraine,' and he was able to play several other tunes quite well.
